title: Round Table Foundation funded by Army, Navy and CIA

tellings.quote: they were just like flocking to this place, basically giving him money to do research. And this was, yeah, '49, '50, very early.

plain: In 1949 and 1950, the Army, the Navy and the CIA were all funding a private research group in Rockland, Maine, called the Round Table Foundation, according to the researcher Greg Malatzi. He tells Michels that the agencies were "flocking to this place, basically giving him money to do research," which means the foundation's head, and he points to letters from the agencies to the foundation. The story matters because it would put the military and the CIA behind fringe research very early on.
